grammar: Cantonese often omits 'to be' in simple descriptions. Instead of saying 'I am hungry', you simply say 'I hungry'. This is normal and natural in Cantonese.

ngo5 m4 tou5 ngo6
nei5 tou5 m4 tou5 ngo6

grammar: Cantonese often uses intensifiers like '好' (very) to express adjectives naturally. Instead of a verb like 'am happy', you say 'I very happy'.

nei5 hoi1 sam1

phrase: I don't want to go out
grammar: Cantonese uses '唔想' to express 'don't want to' or 'don't feel like'. This is more natural than directly translating English structures.

practice.phrase: I really don't want to go out today
practice.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 zan1 hai6 m4 soeng2 ceot1 gaai1

practice.phrase: I don't want to go out because it's too cold
practice.jyutping: taai3 dung3 ngo5 m4 soeng2 ceot1 gaai1

practice.phrase: I still don't want to go out
practice.jyutping: ngo5 dou1 m4 soeng2 ceot1 gaai1

jyutping: ngo5 m4 zung1 ji3 gaa3 fe1
grammar: Cantonese uses '唔鍾意' to express 'don't like'. It is the standard way to express preference or dislike.

practice.phrase: I don't like coffee in the morning
practice.jyutping: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 m4 zung1 ji3 gaa3 fe1
ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 zung1 ji3 gaa3 fe1

practice.phrase: I don't like coffee when it's cold
practice.characters: 凍嘅時候我唔鍾意咖啡
practice.jyutping: dung3 ge3 si4 hau6 ngo5 m4 zung1 ji3 gaa3 fe1

grammar: Cantonese uses '想' (want) + verb directly. There is no need for 'to' as in English. '想食' = want to eat.

practice.phrase: I want to eat rice now
practice.jyutping: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 soeng2 sik6 faan6

practice.phrase: I don't want to eat rice
practice.jyutping: ngo5 m4 soeng2 sik6 faan6

practice.phrase: Do you want to eat rice with me
practice.jyutping: nei5 soeng2 m4 soeng2 tung4 ngo5 sik6 faan6
